title: Passport data vault and airline submission client
name: Passport data submission

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code protects passport numbers at rest or in transit? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. Each encryption uses a fresh random 12-byte IV with AES-256-GCM, stores IV, full 16-byte tag and key id alongside the ciphertext, and binds the booking id as AAD so ciphertexts cannot be swapped between bookings. Decryption checks length and sets the tag before final(). In transit, the agent uses a pinned CA bundle, a client certificate for mutual TLS, TLS 1.2 minimum, and leaves certificate and hostname verification enabled. The error message includes only the booking id, never the passport number.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A stored passport ciphertext for booking BK-1 is copied into the row for booking BK-2. What happens when the supplier client submits BK-2?
choices: The BK-1 passport number is sent for BK-2
decrypt() throws during authentication because the booking id is part of the AAD, so nothing is sent
decrypt() returns an empty string and the supplier rejects the request
needsRotation() returns true and the value is re-encrypted for BK-2
choiceQuestions.explanation: encrypt() and decrypt() both set AAD to booking:<id>; a mismatch makes decipher.final() throw, and submitPassengerData() calls decrypt() while building the body, before any request is made. GCM does not return empty output on failure, and needsRotation() only compares key ids.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Encrypting the same passport number twice for the same booking produces:
choices: Identical strings, so the column can be used for equality lookups
Identical ciphertext bodies but different key ids
Strings that differ only in the auth tag
Different strings, because each call draws a new random IV
choiceQuestions.explanation: randomBytes(IV_BYTES) is called on every encrypt(), so IV, ciphertext and tag all differ. That is why the column cannot support equality lookups; the key id is the same while the current key is unchanged.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The supplier's server stops responding mid-request. How does submitPassengerData() behave?
choices: After timeoutMs of socket inactivity the request is destroyed and the promise rejects with a timeout error
It waits indefinitely because keepAlive sockets have no timeout
It resolves with undefined once the socket closes
It retries on another of the 20 pooled sockets
choiceQuestions.explanation: The request sets timeout: cfg.timeoutMs and the timeout handler destroys the request with an error, which fires the error listener and rejects. keepAlive only affects reuse of idle sockets, there is no resolve path without an end event, and there is no retry logic.
